name_en: Acute Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Common Cold)
name_id: Infeksi Saluran Pernapasan Atas Akut (ISPA)/Common Cold
context_note: Consistently the #1 or #2 outpatient diagnosis at Puskesmas across Java (Jakarta, Central & West Java data); driven by crowding, poor ventilation, tropical climate/pollution.
Among the top 3 outpatient diagnoses in Jakarta puskesmas (283,000+ visits in 2024); a major NCD burden across Java.
Ranked top 3 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas 2024 (202,882 visits); reflects poor oral hygiene access.
One of the top outpatient complaints across Java puskesmas ('sakit maag'); linked to irregular meals, spicy food, stress, H. pylori prevalence.
Top 5 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas (188,000+ visits, 2024); rising prevalence across urban and rural Java.
Top 6 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas 2024 (108,167 visits); complication of poorly controlled chronic hypertension.
Top 7 outpatient diagnosis in Jakarta puskesmas 2024; usually detected on routine screening rather than symptoms.
Frequently reported as 'nyeri sendi/rematik' - among the most common OPD diagnoses at rural Java puskesmas (e.g., top diagnosis at Puskesmas Gabus II 2023).
Consistently in the top 10 across Jakarta and rural Java puskesmas; linked to food/water sanitation.
Listed among Jakarta's top-10 outpatient puskesmas diagnoses (2024); urban Java has established ART programs.
Indonesia has one of the world's highest TB burdens; consistently appears in top-10 puskesmas diagnoses across Java (rural and urban).
Java experiences seasonal dengue outbreaks (rainy season); a frequent cause of acute febrile OPD presentation.
Endemic in Indonesia, especially Java, linked to contaminated food/water; frequent cause of prolonged fever in OPD.
Common chronic respiratory OPD presentation, aggravated by Java's air pollution, dust, and humidity/mold triggers.
A leading cause of respiratory OPD/ER presentation and hospitalization risk, especially in young children and elderly in Java.
Extremely common OPD complaint across Java puskesmas ('maag'/'sakit lambung'), often overlapping with dyspepsia.
Common complaint related to diet (spicy/fatty food), obesity trends, and late-night eating habits.
Common in older OPD patients, especially knee OA, related to age, obesity, and physical labor.
Very common self-reported complaint ('asam urat') in Java OPD, linked to diet high in purines (organ meat, seafood, melinjo).
Less common than OA/gout but an important differential when patients present with 'rematik' - symmetric small joint disease.
One of the most frequent standalone OPD complaints ('sakit kepala'); usually primary headache disorder.
Very common OPD complaint ('pusing berputar'); important to distinguish peripheral (benign) from central (dangerous) causes.
Extremely common complaint, often related to occupation (lifting, prolonged sitting/standing), especially among laborers and market workers.
Common in women of reproductive age and children in Java; linked to nutrition and menstrual blood loss.
Growing OPD burden secondary to poorly controlled hypertension and diabetes across Java.
Common in older patients with smoking history or biomass fuel/cooking smoke exposure, a notable exposure in rural Java kitchens.
Common recurring complaint, often mistaken for chronic 'colds'; triggered by dust mites, humidity, and pollution in Java's climate.
Common in Java's hot, humid climate; frequently aggravated by sweating, soaps, and occupational exposures.
Common in crowded households, boarding schools (pesantren), and dormitories across Java due to close contact transmission.

name_id: Tinea / Infeksi Jamur Kulit (Panu, Kadas, Kurap)
context_note: Very common in Java's hot, humid climate; includes tinea corporis, cruris, pedis, and pityriasis versicolor ('panu').
Common OPD complaint, especially among women; recurrent cases seen with poor hydration/hygiene practices.
Common, especially in children, often following upper respiratory infections; frequent OPD presentation across Java.
Very frequent OPD complaint ('radang tenggorokan'), ranked among top diagnoses at multiple Java puskesmas.
Common, often viral or bacterial, spreads easily in schools/households; frequent 'mata merah' complaint in OPD.
Endemic in parts of Java (e.g., southern coastal areas of Central/East Java, Banten) - important differential for fever in relevant areas/travelers.
Mosquito-borne outbreaks occur periodically across Java; often confused clinically with dengue.
Common especially in children in rural/semi-rural Java, related to sanitation and soil-transmitted helminths (roundworm, whipworm, hookworm).
Notable risk in Java during flooding season (common in Jakarta and other low-lying Java cities); transmitted via rat urine-contaminated water.
Common in areas with limited sanitation infrastructure; periodic outbreaks reported in Java linked to contaminated food/water.
Stroke is a leading cause of disability in Indonesia; many OPD visits are follow-up care for known stroke patients managing risk factors and rehabilitation.
